facts.statement: The genus Acondylacanthus includes eleven described species, such as A. gracilis and A. jaekeli.

facts.statement: Acondylacanthus is an extinct genus belonging to the order Ctenacanthiformes from the Paleozoic era.
facts.quote: Acondylacanthus is an extinct genus of ctenacanthiform from the Paleozoic era.

facts.statement: Most species of Acondylacanthus are known from Carboniferous deposits in America and the British Isles.
facts.quote: Most species are known from the Carboniferous of America and the British isles.

facts.statement: The species A. jaekeli is found in the upper Frasnian of Germany and the Upper Famennian of Russia.
facts.quote: A. jaekeli is known from the upper Frasnian of Germany and the Upper Famennian of Russia.

facts.statement: The genus is defined solely by isolated dorsal fin spines, leading to uncertainty about whether it is synonymous with tooth-based genera.
facts.quote: This genus is based entirely upon isolated dorsal fin spines, and thus may later be found synonymous with tooth-based genera.

facts.statement: Acondylacanthus belongs to the family Ctenacanthidae.
Acondylacanthus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus lived from the Eifelian to the Wuchiapingian, spanning from 393.47 to 254.14 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Eifelian to Wuchiapingian (393.47 to 254.14 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are ten recorded fossil occurrences of Acondylacanthus in the Paleobiology Database.
